Now subtract this approximation from 11 to obtain u~\widetilde{u}, which implies |u~−u|≤η≤u2|\widetilde{u}-u|\leq\eta\leq\frac{u}{2} and thus u~≥u2\widetilde{u}\geq\frac{u}{2}. Therefore by the mean value theorem, for some cc between uu and u~\widetilde{u} we have

|log⁡u~−log⁡u|≤|u~−u|⋅(log⁡t)′​(c)≤η⋅2u≤2−q−2.|\log\widetilde{u}-\log u|\leq|\widetilde{u}-u|\cdot(\log t)^{\prime}(c)\leq\eta\cdot\frac{2}{u}\leq 2^{-q-2}.

Approximate log⁡u~\log\widetilde{u} to an additional error of 2−q−22^{-q-2} via Taylor expansion of log⁡(1−t)\log(1-t), by first scaling the argument u~\widetilde{u} to the interval [12,1][\frac{1}{2},1]. This gives the required approximation to ℓ⁡(s)\ell(s).

The rational term (N−1)​max⁡{t,0}(N-1)\max\{t,0\} has encoding length polynomial in B+log⁡NB+\log N, and errors in the two logarithms add without amplification. Thus HN​(t)H_{N}(t) is computable to error 21−q2^{1-q} in time polynomial in B,log⁡N,qB,\log N,q. Taking

q=⌈log2⁡4​nτ⌉q=\left\lceil\log_{2}\frac{4n}{\tau}\right\rceil

bounds the error in each term of the sum defining Φ⁡(𝒛)\Phi(\bm{z}) by τ2​n\frac{\tau}{2n}; the cases t=0t=0 are evaluated to the same or better accuracy. Exact rational summation produces a rational VV satisfying |V−Φ⁡(z)|≤τ2<τ|V-\Phi(z)|\leq\frac{\tau}{2}<\tau.

Approximate gradients.

Approximate gradients then follow from finite differences, which we now show. First, since 𝒃∈M⁡[𝟎,𝒌]\bm{b}\in M[\bm{0},\bm{k}], let 𝒚∈[𝟎,𝒌]\bm{y}\in[\bm{0},\bm{k}] be such that ∑i=1nyi​𝒂i=𝒃\sum_{i=1}^{n}y_{i}\bm{a}_{i}=\bm{b}. For fixed kk and tt, the first and second derivatives of Hk+1H_{k+1} are the mean and variance of the distribution μ\mu supported on {0,…,k}\{0,\ldots,k\} with probabilities μℓ∝eℓ​t\mu_{\ell}\propto e^{\ell t}. Since μ\mu is supported on {0,…,k}\{0,\ldots,k\}, this implies

‖∇Φ​(𝒛)‖2=‖∑j=1n𝒂j​[Hkj+1′​(𝒂j⊤​𝒛)−yj]‖2≤L:=m​∑j=1nkj.\|\nabla\Phi(\bm{z})\|_{2}=\left\|\sum_{j=1}^{n}\bm{a}_{j}\left[H_{k_{j}+1}^{\prime}(\bm{a}_{j}^{\top}\bm{z})-y_{j}\right]\right\|_{2}\leq L:=\sqrt{m}\sum_{j=1}^{n}k_{j}.

and

0⪯∇2Φ(𝒛)=∑j=1n𝒂j𝒂j⊤Hkj+1′′(𝒂j⊤𝒛)⪯I⋅m∑j=1nkj2,0\preceq\nabla^{2}\Phi(\bm{z})=\sum_{j=1}^{n}\bm{a}_{j}\bm{a}_{j}^{\top}H_{k_{j}+1}^{\prime\prime}(\bm{a}_{j}^{\top}\bm{z})\preceq I\cdot m\sum_{j=1}^{n}k_{j}^{2},

so that

‖∇2Φ​(𝒛)‖op≤H:=m​∑j=1nkj2.\|\nabla^{2}\Phi(\bm{z})\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq H:=m\sum_{j=1}^{n}k_{j}^{2}.

For coordinatewise gradient error δ\delta, evaluate Φ⁡(𝒛)\Phi(\bm{z}) and Φ⁡(𝒛+h​𝒆i)\Phi(\bm{z}+h\bm{e}_{i}), so that

|∂ziΦ⁡(𝒛)−Φ⁡(𝒛+h​𝒆i)−Φ⁡(𝒛)h|≤H​h2.\left|\partial_{z_{i}}\Phi(\bm{z})-\frac{\Phi(\bm{z}+h\bm{e}_{i})-\Phi(\bm{z})}{h}\right|\leq\frac{Hh}{2}.

Approximating Φ⁡(𝒛)\Phi(\bm{z}) by V0V_{0} and Φ⁡(𝒛+h​𝒆i)\Phi(\bm{z}+h\bm{e}_{i}) by ViV_{i} within error τ\tau (as described above) then implies Vi−V0h\frac{V_{i}-V_{0}}{h} is within error 2​τh\frac{2\tau}{h}. This implies

|∂ziΦ⁡(𝒛)−Vi−V0h|≤H​h2+2​τh\left|\partial_{z_{i}}\Phi(\bm{z})-\frac{V_{i}-V_{0}}{h}\right|\leq\frac{Hh}{2}+\frac{2\tau}{h}

Taking h=δ4​Hh=\frac{\delta}{4H} and τ=δ​h8=δ232​H\tau=\frac{\delta h}{8}=\frac{\delta^{2}}{32H}, this implies an overall error of H​h2+2​τh=δ8+δ4<δ\frac{Hh}{2}+\frac{2\tau}{h}=\frac{\delta}{8}+\frac{\delta}{4}<\delta. Note that HH is polynomial in mm and 𝒌\bm{k}, and thus log⁡1τ\log\frac{1}{\tau} depends polynomially on log⁡m\log m, log⁡(1+‖𝒌‖1)\log(1+\|\bm{k}\|_{1}), and log⁡1δ\log\frac{1}{\delta}.

The algorithm.

We now apply the approximate-oracle ellipsoid implementation of Section 6.2 (of the arXiv version) of [41] (see also Theorem 2.13), using the preceding bounds on the search region and the Lipschitz constant LL of Φ\Phi. The value and gradient oracles established above provide its required numerical approximations. The number of oracle calls and the required number of accuracy bits are polynomial in the input length and log⁡1ϵ\log\frac{1}{\epsilon}. Since our oracles run in time polynomial in these quantities and the encoding length of the query point, the resulting algorithm finds 𝒛∘\bm{z}^{\circ} satisfying

Φ⁡(𝒛∘)≤min⁡Φ+ϵ2\Phi(\bm{z}^{\circ})\leq\min\Phi+\frac{\epsilon}{2}

in polynomial bit complexity. Evaluating Φ⁡(𝒛∘)\Phi(\bm{z}^{\circ}) to additive error ϵ2\frac{\epsilon}{2} then gives a rational 𝒜\mathcal{A} with |𝒜−log⁡ℰ|≤ϵ|\mathcal{A}-\log\mathcal{E}|\leq\epsilon.

We note that although the total running time stated in [41] depends polynomially on 1ϵ\frac{1}{\epsilon}, its ellipsoid iteration bound depends only polynomially on log⁡1ε\log\frac{1}{\varepsilon} (see Section 6.2, immediately before Lemma 6.3). The worse dependence comes from the approximate-counting oracle used there. Our value and gradient oracles instead run in time polynomial in the number of requested accuracy bits, so the same optimization framework gives polynomial dependence on log⁡1ε\log\frac{1}{\varepsilon} in our setting.
